images.title: Even side or both odd?
images.purpose: Compare the three cases of an m × n grid: both sides even, one side even, and both sides odd.
images.composition: Three small grids side by side with equal spacing, each with a short label above and a size label, tick or cross below, on a white background.
exact_structure: Left: a grid of 6 rows and 4 columns, covered by exactly 12 vertical 2 × 1 tiles (3 in each of the 4 columns), filled teal (#0072B2) with thick dark outlines; label above: both even; label below: 6 × 4; a green (#009E73) tick under it.

Middle: a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, covered by exactly 6 horizontal 2 × 1 tiles (2 in each of the 3 rows), filled amber (#E69F00) with thick dark outlines; label above: one even; label below: 3 × 4; a green (#009E73) tick under it.
Right: a grid of 3 rows and 5 columns of 15 empty white squares with thin grey (#6B7280) lines and no tiles; label above: both odd; label below: 3 × 5 = 15; a vermilion (#D55E00) cross under it.
All unit squares are the same size in the three grids.
rejection: any grid with the wrong number of rows or columns (6 by 4, 3 by 4, 3 by 5)
tiles drawn on the 3 × 5 grid, or a tick under the 3 × 5 grid
the 6 × 4 grid not using exactly 12 tiles or the 3 × 4 grid not using exactly 6 tiles
images.takeaway: If either side is even, line up the tiles along it; if both sides are odd, the number of squares is odd and no tiling exists.
images.description: Three grids in a row: a 6 by 4 grid tiled with vertical tiles, a 3 by 4 grid tiled with horizontal tiles, and an untiled 3 by 5 grid with a cross.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on which m × n grids can be tiled.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which side is even in each tiled grid and notice that the tiles run along that side.

image_decisions.why: Three grids side by side make the even, mixed and odd cases easy to compare.
